minecraft_java.description: Minecraft is a creative building game. Think digital LEGO. Children explore a blocky world, gather materials and build whatever they imagine, from a cosy house to a whole city. There is no winning or losing. It is a calm, open-ended space to create and solve problems. “Java” is the original version for Windows, Mac and Linux computers. It is the one our remote clubs use, because it supports the tools our Game Educators rely on.
minecraft_java.note: For our remote clubs your child needs Minecraft on a computer. On Minecraft’s own site it is sold as “Minecraft: Java & Bedrock Edition for PC”. That is a single one-time purchase rather than a subscription, and it includes the version we use. The separate console, phone and tablet version does not work for these clubs.

minecraft_bedrock.description: Minecraft is a creative building game. Think digital LEGO. Children explore a blocky world, gather materials and build whatever they imagine, from a cosy house to a whole city. There is no winning or losing. It is a calm, open-ended space to create and solve problems. “Bedrock” is the version that runs on consoles (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch), phones, tablets and Windows PCs.
minecraft_bedrock.note: Minecraft Bedrock is not included in the price. It is the same game sold separately for each device, and a copy bought for one device does not carry over to another. The copy that counts is the one for the device your child will play on. On a games console, playing online also needs that console’s paid online membership.

minecraft_education.description: Minecraft is a creative building game. Think digital LEGO. Children explore a blocky world, gather materials and build whatever they imagine. Minecraft Education is a version built for guided groups. It is the same friendly, open-ended building, with extra tools for the adult running the session.
minecraft_education.note: There is nothing to buy and no school account to arrange. School of Gaming provides the Minecraft Education accounts participants use during the sessions. For remote clubs the game itself is a free download from the Microsoft Store or from Minecraft Education’s own site. It runs on Windows and Mac computers as well as iPads and Chromebooks.

fortnite.description: Fortnite is a colourful, cartoon-style online game where players team up and compete in short, round-based matches. It is hugely popular and very social, and children play it together with friends. The look is bright and non-realistic, with no blood or gore. Matches are competitive and played online with other people.
fortnite.note: Fortnite is free to download and play, so there is no game to buy. Playing needs a free Epic Games account. Some optional extras cost money, such as outfits. Epic’s parental controls sit on the account rather than on a device, and they can limit those extras.

pokemon_go.description: Pokémon GO is played outdoors, on a phone. Creatures appear on a map of the real world, and children walk to parks, streets and landmarks to find and collect them. It is about collecting rather than fighting. The appeal is exploring, filling up a Pokédex and comparing finds with friends. Most of the playing happens on foot, so it tends to get children moving.
pokemon_go.note: Pokémon GO is free to download and play, so there is no game to buy. It needs a phone with GPS and a mobile data connection, plus a free account. For a child under 13 the account is created by a parent and stays linked to theirs. There are optional in-app purchases, which parental controls can limit. It is played outdoors in real places. It also keeps the screen, GPS and data running the whole time, so a battery does not last long.

roblox_studio.description: Roblox Studio is the free tool that Roblox games themselves are made with. Children design worlds, build with real 3D tools and write real code. They turn their own ideas into experiences other people can actually play. In our clubs they create rather than play, which is a first step into real game development.
roblox_studio.note: Roblox Studio is free, so there is nothing to buy. It runs on Windows PCs and Macs only, not on an iPad or other tablet, not on a Chromebook, phone or games console. A free Roblox account is needed too, and the account’s age setting governs its chat and privacy controls. Finished creations can be published for other players to find and play.

rocket_league.description: Rocket League is football played with rocket-powered cars. Two teams drive around an arena and try to push an oversized ball into the other team’s goal, in short matches of about five minutes. The look is bright and cartoonish and there is no violence. It is a sport, not a shooter, so it is easy to follow from the sidelines even if you have never played it yourself. Almost every goal comes out of the team working together, which is why it suits club play so well.
rocket_league.note: Rocket League is free to download and play, so there is no game to buy. Playing needs a free Epic Games account. It runs on Windows PCs, PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo Switch. Players on different devices can play together, so your child’s device does not have to match anyone else’s. There are optional in-game purchases (decorations for the cars), which parental controls can limit.
